incumbent.text: Hypothesis: a real multiline private-key block survives because the PEM regex expects literal backslash-n separators and only a generic header. Applicability: the central formatter is attached to file logging, and the analyst may call it directly on a disposable string. Bounded test: emit generic, RSA, and ENCRYPTED blocks with real newlines and a base64 marker, plus a literal-backslash-n control. Expected result: base64 markers disappear and END headers remain; falsifier: any marker survives. Cleanup: delete the temporary log and fixture key material.

hint: A Python connector's central formatter masks tokens, passwords, cloud keys, signed-URL signatures, JSON token values, and private-key-data fields. A first probe showed real-newline generic, RSA, and ENCRYPTED private-key blocks leaking, while a literal-backslash-n generic block was masked; six-digit passcode/auth_code/mfa_code values and authorization-scheme headers also leaked. A real-newline header/body/footer span is now the leading repair candidate. Question: which implementation closes the private-key gap with the least benign over-masking, and which companion pattern is needed for short codes?
